use_case: Revenue-management pricing: machine-learning demand forecasts and room rate recommendations that publish automatically for 110 company-operated hotels, also offered to franchisees as the franchise pricing service (212 subscribing franchised hotels)
business_owner: Chief Commercial Officer (operated by the Vice President, Revenue Strategy)
vendor_or_model: Revenue-management vendor (machine-learning forecasting and pricing SaaS)
data_categories: Aggregated bookings, stay history, and rates from the CRS and PMS; public competitor rates; events calendar. Vendor contract allows pooling of non-public rate and occupancy data across client hotels into a benchmark
affects_individuals: Yes (prices paid by guests; not individualized)
consequential_decision_category: None (room prices are not a listed consequential decision); treated as High in a declared state of emergency
human_in_the_loop: Automatic publishing within floor, ceiling, and daily change limits at company-operated hotels; revenue managers approve exceptions. Franchisees set their own guardrails and approve or reject recommendations
applicable_laws: FTC Act Section 5 (15 U.S.C. 45(a), (n)); 16 CFR 464.2 (total price in feeds and displays); Fla. Stat. 501.160 and other state price gouging laws in declared emergencies; Sherman Act Section 1 (15 U.S.C. 1) litigation risk from pooled non-public data
bias_testing_status: Quote parity test across locations, devices, languages, and member status (120 quotes, no unexplained differences)
monitoring: Daily exception report; monthly guardrail breaches; emergency-mode events; quarterly quote parity test

use_case: Guest chatbot on the brand website, app, and messaging: answers questions, quotes availability and rates, looks up the signed-in member's own reservations, and links to the booking engine (also used on SL-2 client booking pages)
business_owner: Chief Commercial Officer (operated by the Vice President, Digital and Loyalty)
vendor_or_model: Company-built integration on Cloud provider B's managed generative AI service (third-party large language model)
data_categories: Guest questions, names, contact details, and transcripts; availability and rates from the CRS; member reservations. Card numbers redacted before storage since 2026-07
human_in_the_loop: Staff handoff for booking changes, complaints, accessibility, medical, and emergency questions; weekly review of 100 transcripts
applicable_laws: 16 CFR 464.2 and 464.3 (total price; fee descriptions); FTC Act Section 5 (accuracy of answers and AI claims); PCI DSS v4.0.1 (card numbers in chat); state breach laws for transcripts (Fla. Stat. 501.171 worked example); state AI disclosure-on-request rules
bias_testing_status: English and Spanish test sets monthly (gap found)
monitoring: Monthly 200-question accuracy test; monthly total price test; weekly transcript review; handoff rate

use_case: Contact center agent assist: call transcription, summaries, and suggested answers for about 650 agents
vendor_or_model: Contact center platform vendor (generative speech and language features)
data_categories: Call audio and transcripts (card digits never reach agents because of tone masking); reservation data
human_in_the_loop: Agents choose whether to use suggestions; supervisors review 20 calls per agent a month
applicable_laws: FTC Act Section 5; state call recording consent laws (all-party notice at call start); PCI DSS v4.0.1 (no card data in transcripts)
bias_testing_status: Summary accuracy by caller language (English, Spanish) quarterly
monitoring: Monthly summary accuracy sample; transcript card-data scan

use_case: Booking fraud and card-testing detection on the booking engine: risk scores that challenge or decline suspicious bookings
business_owner: Director of Payments and PCI Compliance
vendor_or_model: Payment fraud screening vendor (machine-learning risk scoring)
data_categories: Booking details, device and network signals, card tokens
affects_individuals: Yes (guests whose bookings are challenged or declined)
consequential_decision_category: None (booking decline is not a listed consequential decision)
human_in_the_loop: Declines above the score threshold are automatic; challenged bookings go to the fraud team; guests can book by phone
applicable_laws: FTC Act Section 5; PCI DSS v4.0.1; state privacy laws for device data
bias_testing_status: False decline rate by card-issuing country and device type quarterly
monitoring: Daily fraud and decline dashboards; chargeback rate

use_case: Mobile check-in identity verification: matches a guest selfie to the identity document photo before issuing a digital key
vendor_or_model: Identity verification vendor (face matching and document authentication)
data_categories: Selfie and identity document images; face templates (deleted within 24 hours by contract); match scores
consequential_decision_category: None listed, but it controls issuance of a room key (physical security)
human_in_the_loop: Failed or low-confidence matches go to the front desk for in-person check-in; no guest is refused a stay by the tool
applicable_laws: State biometric laws (disabled in Illinois; 740 ILCS 14 not re-verified); Fla. Stat. 501.171(1)(g)1.a.(VI) and 501.702 definition (whether templates from photos are biometric data is unsettled; treated as biometric data); FTC Act Section 5
bias_testing_status: Vendor accuracy data only; local testing by age band and skin tone due 2027-03-31 (POAM-020)
monitoring: Monthly false rejection rate; quarterly vendor deletion attestation
